title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-34
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops
Date created: 2026-03-03    last edited: 2026-03-04

Quick summary:
- Small day: focus on capacity sizing for Q2, follow up on node networking flakiness, triage one noisy pod causing GPU memory fragmentation.
- Priorities: finalize capacity calc for batch-runner, finish PR for instance warm-up, confirm VPC SG changes with infra-networking.

Checks to run (quick commands):
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 5  # watch problem nodes
- dcgmi dmon  # if DCGM enabled on node
- kubectl top pod -n inference | grep -E "batch-runner|launcher"
- kubectl logs -n inference gateway-xyz -c model-server --tail 200 | grep -i oom  # check for OOMs
- check /var/log/inference/gpu-monitor.log for repeated allocation failures

Capacity notes (Q2 reserve planning):
- Current avg sustained GPU-hours: ~18k/wk across hosted and dedicated pools. Burst factor 1.6 during peak (US morning).
- Target: add +12 A100s to dedicated-pool-2 to keep p95 latency within 350ms for prompt-length <=1024.
- Options: reserve 8 A100s + enable autoscale burst of 4 on dedicated-pool-2 (cheaper than full reserve). Recommend cost calc in GH PR.
- Action: update spreadsheet with updated runrate and expected savings from prefix caching. Linked spreadsheet: confluence:infra/gpu-capacity-plans

Networking reminders / flakiness:
- Observed intermittent packet drops between us-west-2 gpu-allocator nodes and storage (S3 proxy). Suspect MTU mismatch after recent SR-IOV changes.
- Repro steps: run iperf3 between node A and B for 10m, check for retransmits.
- Temp workaround: pin inter-pod traffic to CNI-plugin version v1.4.2 on affected nodes.
- Follow-up: sync with Marco/Rachel from infra-networking. Opened JIRA-2148.

Incident / triage notes:
- No major incidents today. One noisy pod (batch-runner-7) triggered eviction cascades on node gpunode-17 yesterday 03/02 21:12 UTC. Root cause: memory leak in python worker (float64 buffer not freed).
- Mitigation applied: restarted pod, rolled back to image v2.3.1 (pre-allocator-change). Created GH:infra/gpu-allocator#89 for fix (WIP).

TODO (ordered):
- [ ] Finalize capacity numbers and submit reserve recommendation PR (due 2026-03-06). Owner: Alex.
- [ ] Add autoscale test that simulates 2x traffic spike and verify p95 stays < 350ms. Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Run iperf3 between affected nodes and capture logs; share with infra-networking. Owner: Alex.
- [ ] Merge warm-up instance PR after one more perf run. Owner: Marco.
- [ ] Add a quick alert for repeated "allocation failed" messages in /var/log/inference/gpu-monitor.log (threshold: 5 in 10m). Owner: Alex.

Notes to self / misc:
- Remember to add note about quantization tradeoffs to capacity doc - smaller model variants reduce memory pressure but increase CPU decode time on some configs.
- Check with product-hosted-api about rolling new model variant that uses 8-bit quantization; impact on latency must be measured.
- Keep an eye on cost dashboard for dedicated-pool-2 - anomalies last week correlated with cache TTL change.
- If seeing repeated OOMs after rollout, escalate to on-call SRE and consider temporary scale-up of dedicated nodes.

Meeting follow-ups:
- 2026-03-04 10:00 sync with infra-networking: confirm whether SR-IOV revert is feasible for small subset of nodes.
- 2026-03-05 16:00 capacity review with Eng leads - finalize numbers before sales sync.

Short log of actions taken (timestamps in UTC):
- 2026-03-03 09:15: ran nvidia-smi sweep on dedicated-pool-2, noticed 2 nodes with high mem fragmentation.
- 2026-03-03 11:40: restarted batch-runner-7 on gpunode-17; temp mitigation applied.
- 2026-03-03 14:05: opened GH:infra/gpu-allocator#89 and linked JIRA-2148.

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc as working notes - will prune into capacity plan doc once numbers stabilized.
